questions.question: All eukaryotic cells are supported structurally by an internal network of proteins known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cytoskeleton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The **cytoskeleton** is an internal network of protein filaments and tubules present in all eukaryotic cells.

• It provides **structural support** to the cell, maintaining its shape and organization.

• The cytoskeleton is composed of three primary components: **microfilaments** (actin filaments), **microtubules**, and **intermediate filaments**.

• This network is involved in various cellular processes, including **intracellular transport**, cell division (mitosis and meiosis), and cell signaling.

• The cytoskeleton plays a crucial role in **cell motility**, enabling cells to move and change shape during processes like wound healing and immune responses.

questions.question: What is the boiling point of water at sea level?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**212 ºF**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **boiling point of water** at sea level is **212 ºF**, which is equivalent to **100 ºC**.
 
• This boiling point is determined under **standard atmospheric pressure**, which is approximately **1 atmosphere (101.325 kPa).**
 
• At this temperature, water transitions from the **liquid phase to the gas phase**, forming steam.
 
• The boiling point of water can change with variations in **altitude and atmospheric pressure.** For example, at higher altitudes, where the atmospheric pressure is lower, water boils at a temperature **below 212 ºF.**
 
• Boiling water is crucial in various **scientific, industrial, and daily applications,** such as cooking, sterilization, and generating steam for energy production.
 
• The boiling point of water is often used as a reference point in **thermometry** and other scientific measurements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Altitude and Boiling Point Relationship**__

 __
 
• As altitude increases, the **atmospheric pressure decreases**, which reduces the boiling point of water.
 
• For example, at an altitude of around **5,000 feet**, water boils at approximately **203 ºF.**
 
• This principle is significant in **mountainous regions** and affects cooking times for food preparation.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Boiling Water**__
 
 
• Boiling water is widely used for **purification** and sterilization to kill harmful microbes.
 
• It is a key component in **steam engines**, which were historically significant in industrial development.
 
• Boiling water plays an essential role in **scientific experiments** and chemical processes.

questions.question: What role do teeth play in the digestion of food?

options.text: They crush and grind the food into smaller particles
They absorb nutrients from the food

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They crush and grind the food into smaller particles**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary role of **teeth** in the digestive system is **mechanical digestion**. They physically break down large pieces of food into smaller particles through the process of **mastication** (chewing).
 
• By crushing and grinding food, teeth increase the **surface area** of the food, which allows **digestive enzymes** in the saliva and stomach to work more efficiently.
 
• **Secreting enzymes** is not a function of teeth; this is done by various **glands** such as the salivary glands, stomach lining, and pancreas.
 
• **Saliva production** is the responsibility of the **salivary glands** (parotid, submandibular, and sublingual), not the teeth.
 
• **Nutrient absorption** occurs primarily in the **small intestine**, where the lining is specialized to transport nutrients into the bloodstream.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Humans have four main types of teeth: **Incisors** for cutting, **Canines** for tearing, and **Premolars** and **Molars** for grinding and crushing.
 
• The outermost layer of the tooth is called **enamel**, which is the **hardest substance** in the human body and protects the tooth from wear and tear.
 
• The human dental formula for permanent teeth is **2:1:2:3**, representing the number of incisors, canines, premolars, and molars in one quadrant of the mouth.
 
• **Mechanical digestion** begins in the **mouth** with the teeth and tongue, while **chemical digestion** begins simultaneously as **salivary amylase** starts breaking down carbohydrates.

questions.question: The International Space Station is a large space station in low earth orbit at about ____ Km from the Earth surface.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**400**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** is a modular space station located in **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**. It orbits at an average altitude of approximately **400 kilometers** (roughly **250 miles**) above the **Earth's surface**.
 
• It travels at a velocity of approximately **28,000 kilometers per hour** (**17,500 miles per hour**). At this incredible speed, the **ISS** completes one full orbit of the **Earth** every **90 to 93 minutes**, meaning the astronauts on board witness about **16 sunrises and sunsets** every **24 hours**.
 
• The construction of the station began in **1998** with the launch of the **Russian** module **Zarya**. Since then, various modules have been added by different participating nations to expand its living and laboratory space.
 
• The altitude of the **ISS** is not fixed; it fluctuates between **330 km** and **435 km** due to **atmospheric drag**. To maintain its orbit and prevent it from crashing into the atmosphere, the station requires periodic "re-boosts" using its own engines or those of docked spacecraft.
 
• The **ISS** serves as a unique **microgravity** and space environment research laboratory where scientific contributions are made in **astrobiology**, **astronomy**, **meteorology**, and **physics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Collaboration:** The **ISS** is a joint project involving five participating space agencies: **NASA** (United States), **Roscosmos** (Russia), **JAXA** (Japan), **ESA** (Europe), and **CSA** (Canada). The ownership and use of the station are established by intergovernmental treaties and agreements.
 
• **Physical Characteristics:** The station is roughly the size of a **football field**, measuring about **109 meters** in length. It features large **solar arrays** that collect energy from the **Sun** to power its various systems and scientific experiments.
 
• **Human Occupation:** The **ISS** has been continuously inhabited since **November 2, 2000**. This represents the longest continuous human presence in **space**, surpassing the previous record held by the **Russian** space station **Mir**.
 
• **Scientific Utility:** One of the primary goals of the **ISS** is to provide a platform for long-term research that cannot be performed on **Earth**. This includes studying the effects of long-term **spaceflight** on the **human body**, which is critical for future missions to the **Moon** and **Mars**.
 
• **Observation from Earth:** Due to its size and the reflectivity of its **solar panels**, the **ISS** is the **third brightest object** in the night sky after the **Moon** and **Venus**. It can be seen with the naked eye from the ground as a steady, moving point of light.
 
• **Comparison with Other Orbits:**
 
 
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO):** Extends up to **2,000 km**. This is where most satellites and the **ISS** reside.
 
• **Medium Earth Orbit (MEO):** Ranges from **2,000 km** to **35,786 km**. **GPS** satellites typically operate here at about **20,200 km**.
 
• **Geostationary Orbit (GEO):** Located at exactly **35,786 km**. Satellites here appear stationary over a fixed point on **Earth**, used mostly for **telecommunications** and **weather monitoring**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Microgravity:** Often mistakenly called "zero gravity," the **ISS** is actually in a state of **freefall**. The **gravity** at that altitude is still about **90%** of that on **Earth's surface**, but the station's forward motion keeps it falling "around" the planet rather than into it.
 
• **Water Recycling:** Because resources are limited, the **ISS** uses advanced life support systems that recycle about **93%** of all water on board, including **urine** and **sweat**, converting it back into drinkable water.
 
• **Zvezda Module:** This is the functional center of the **Russian** segment, providing life support systems and the engines used for **orbital altitude** adjustments.

questions.question: The magnitude of buoyant force depends on the _________ of the fluid.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**density**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Buoyant force** is the upward force exerted by a fluid on an object submerged in it. This force enables objects to float or rise in fluids.

• The magnitude of buoyant force depends on the **density of the fluid**. Higher fluid density results in a greater buoyant force.

• According to **Archimedes' principle**, the buoyant force is equal to the weight of the displaced fluid. The weight of the displaced fluid is determined by its density and volume.

• The formula for buoyant force is: **Fb = ρ × V × g**, where **ρ** is the density of the fluid, **V** is the volume of displaced fluid, and **g** is the acceleration due to gravity.

• Other properties like **refractive index**, **colour**, or **charge** do not influence buoyant force. These are unrelated to the physical interaction between the object and fluid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Archimedes' Principle:** 

• It states that any object fully or partially submerged in a fluid experiences a buoyant force equal to the weight of the displaced fluid.

• This principle is applicable to both liquids and gases.

• It was discovered by the Greek mathematician and inventor **Archimedes** around 250 BC.

• **Density:**

• Density is defined as mass per unit volume: **ρ = m/V**.

• Units of density are typically expressed in **kg/m³** or **g/cm³**.

• Examples: Water has a density of **1000 kg/m³**, while air has a density of approximately **1.225 kg/m³** at sea level.

• **Applications of Buoyant Force:**

• **Shipbuilding:** Large ships float because their design ensures the weight of displaced water is greater than the weight of the ship.

• **Submarines:** Submarines adjust their buoyancy by controlling water and air in ballast tanks.

• **Hot Air Balloons:** The buoyant force from the surrounding cooler air lifts the balloon filled with heated air.

• **Factors Affecting Buoyant Force:**

• **Density of Fluid:** Higher density fluids exert greater buoyant force.

• **Volume of Object Submerged:** Larger submerged volume displaces more fluid and increases buoyant force.

• **Gravitational Acceleration:** Variations in gravity influence buoyant force magnitude (e.g., weaker gravity on the Moon).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Refractive Index:** 

• This property measures how much light bends when it enters a material. It has no connection to buoyant force.

• **Colour:** 

• Colour is a visual property determined by the wavelength of light reflected by an object or fluid. It does not affect buoyancy.

• **Charge:** 

• Charge refers to the electrical property of particles. It does not interact with buoyant force, which is a mechanical phenomenon.

questions.question: Which of the following phenomena occurs when a wave passes through a narrow slit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diffraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Diffraction** is the bending of waves around obstacles or the spreading of waves as they pass through narrow slits or openings.
 
• The phenomenon is more pronounced when the size of the slit or obstacle is comparable to the wavelength of the wave.
 
• Diffraction occurs for all types of waves, including light waves, sound waves, and water waves.
 
• This bending allows waves to propagate into the geometrical shadow region, creating interference patterns.
 
• In optics, diffraction effects are essential in understanding the behavior of light in devices such as diffraction gratings and optical instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wavelength:** The distance between consecutive crests or troughs of a wave. Diffraction depends on the wavelength relative to the size of the slit or obstacle.
 
• **Interference Patterns:** Diffraction often produces constructive and destructive interference patterns, leading to regions of bright and dark fringes.
 
• **Huygens' Principle:** A foundational principle in wave optics stating that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets, which combine to form the observed wave.
 
• **Applications of Diffraction:** Used in X-ray crystallography to determine atomic structures, and in spectrometers and diffraction gratings for analyzing light spectra.
 
• **Double-Slit Experiment:** A classic demonstration of diffraction and interference, highlighting the wave nature of light and other particles.

questions.question: What type of radiation is responsible for ionizing atmospheric gases in the Earth's ionosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ultraviolet Radiation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ionosphere** is a region of the Earth's upper atmosphere, extending from approximately 60 km to 1,000 km above the surface, where the air is ionized by solar energy.
 
• **Ultraviolet (UV) radiation** from the Sun is the primary agent responsible for this ionization. UV photons possess sufficient energy to knock electrons out of the atoms and molecules of atmospheric gases (such as **oxygen** and **nitrogen**), creating a layer of **free electrons** and **positive ions**.
 
• While **Solar Radiation** is the broad term for all energy emitted by the Sun, **Ultraviolet Radiation** (along with X-rays) is the specific component of the electromagnetic spectrum that drives the ionization process in the upper atmosphere.
 
• **Cosmic Radiation**, which originates from outside the solar system, does contribute to ionization, but its effect is significantly smaller than that of solar UV radiation within the ionosphere.
 
• **Gamma Radiation** is highly energetic but is not the primary source for the sustained ionization layers found in the Earth's ionosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ionosphere is critical for **radio communication** because it reflects **high-frequency (HF)** or shortwave radio waves back to Earth, allowing for long-distance transmission beyond the horizon.
 
• It is composed of several layers, known as the **D, E, and F layers**. The **F layer** (also known as the **Appleton-Barnett layer**) has the highest electron density and is most important for skywave propagation.
 
• Ionization levels fluctuate based on the **diurnal cycle** (day and night), seasons, and the 11-year **solar cycle**. During the night, the D and E layers largely disappear as ions and electrons recombine in the absence of solar UV.
 
• Phenomena such as the **Aurora Borealis** (Northern Lights) occur when charged particles from the solar wind interact with the gases in the ionosphere near the Earth's magnetic poles.

questions.question: Why is it more difficult to walk on sand than on a concrete pavement?

options.text: Sand has a higher coefficient of static friction than concrete.
Sand is less dense than concrete, causing less gravitational pull.
Sand particles are magnetic, creating an opposing force.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sand displaces, reducing pushback**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

• **Sand displaces under pressure:** When you walk on sand, the particles beneath your feet shift and move apart. This displacement reduces the ability of the sand to provide a firm surface for pushback, making walking more difficult. *Hence, this explains the correct answer.* 

• **Concrete provides a rigid surface:** Unlike sand, concrete is a solid, immovable surface. It does not shift or deform under pressure, allowing for greater pushback and making walking easier. 

• **Lack of resistance on sand:** Sand does not offer as much resistance as concrete because it is composed of loose particles that can easily rearrange. This lack of resistance makes walking on sand more effort-intensive.

questions.question:
Read the below statements about transpiration:

1. Transpiration is highest in dry and windy conditions.

2. It helps in the ascent of sap through cohesion-tension.

3. Transpiration always results in wilting. Which of the above statements are **correct**?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: Only 1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Transpiration is highest in dry and windy conditions because these conditions enhance the evaporation of water from the leaf surface, increasing the transpiration rate.
 
• **Statement 2:** Transpiration helps in the ascent of sap through the plant’s vascular system by creating a negative pressure in the xylem, which is supported by the cohesion-tension theory.
 
• The process of transpiration is essential for water movement in plants as it aids in nutrient uptake and maintains plant temperature.
 
• Both statements 1 and 2 are scientifically correct and aligned with modern botanical principles.
 
• **Statement 3 is incorrect:** Transpiration does not always result in wilting. Wilting occurs only when water loss due to transpiration exceeds the water absorption by roots, leading to a water deficit in plant cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transpiration:**
 
 
• It is the process by which plants lose water vapor through stomata in their leaves.
 
• Transpiration plays a critical role in nutrient transport, temperature regulation, and maintaining water balance in plants.
 
• Factors like temperature, humidity, wind speed, and soil water availability influence the rate of transpiration.
 
 
 
• **About Statement 3:**
 
 
• Wilting occurs when transpiration exceeds water absorption, leading to a loss of turgor pressure in plant cells.
 
• However, in normal conditions, plants regulate transpiration effectively and do not wilt.
 
• Guard cells play a key role in controlling the opening and closing of stomata to balance water loss and gas exchange.
 
 
 
• **Cohesion-Tension Theory:**
 
 
• It explains the movement of water through the xylem of plants.
 
• Water molecules are cohesive (stick to each other) and adhesive (stick to xylem walls), enabling the ascent of sap.
 
• Transpiration creates a negative pressure in the leaves, pulling water upward from the roots.
 
 
 
• **Dry and Windy Conditions:**
 
 
• Low humidity and high wind speed increase the water vapor concentration gradient between the leaf and the surrounding air, enhancing transpiration.

questions.question: In May 2025, scientists have created the first 'pangenome' of which crop, an important staple food in Asia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• In **May 2025**, scientists successfully created the first-ever **'pangenome' of Rice**, which marks a significant milestone in agricultural genomics. 
• **Rice** is a vital staple food, particularly in **Asia**, where it constitutes a major part of the daily diet for billions of people. 
• A **'pangenome'** represents the complete set of genes found across multiple varieties of a species, providing a comprehensive genetic blueprint for enhancing crop yield, disease resistance, and adaptability. 
• The creation of the rice pangenome is expected to help breeders and researchers develop **climate-resilient rice varieties** and improve food security in the face of global challenges such as climate change. 
• This breakthrough highlights the importance of rice as a global food crop and the role of advanced genomic research in ensuring sustainable agricultural practices. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **What is a Pangenome?** 
• A **Pangenome** is the collection of all the genes present in different varieties or populations of a species, including core genes (common across all varieties) and accessory genes (unique to specific varieties). 
• Pangenomes help researchers identify genetic diversity, allowing for targeted improvements in crop traits such as yield, disease resistance, and environmental adaptability. 
• **Importance of Rice:** 
• Rice is a staple food for more than **50% of the world's population**, particularly in **Asia**, where countries like India, China, and Japan are among the largest producers and consumers. 
• It provides essential **carbohydrates** and is a primary source of nutrition in many developing countries. 
• Rice farming supports the livelihoods of millions of farmers worldwide, making it a critical agricultural commodity. 
• **Other Crops:** 
• **Maize:** A staple food and feed crop widely grown in **North America, Africa, and South America**. It is used for food, animal feed, and industrial applications. 
• **Barley:** Primarily cultivated in **Europe and North America**, barley is used for malting, food, and fodder purposes. 
• **Wheat:** A key cereal crop grown in **temperate regions** globally, it is a major ingredient in bread, pasta, and other food products. 
• **Significance of Genomic Research in Agriculture:** 
• Advanced genomic studies, like the creation of pangenomes, enable the identification of genetic traits that improve crop performance and resilience. 
• These developments are crucial in addressing challenges such as **climate change, pest outbreaks, and increasing global food demand**. 
• They also support the development of sustainable agricultural practices, ensuring long-term food security. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Rice Production in Asia:** 
• Asia accounts for over **90% of global rice production**, with countries like **India, China, Indonesia, and Thailand** being major producers. 
• Rice cultivation is heavily dependent on **irrigation and monsoon rainfall**, making it sensitive to climate change impacts. 
• **Applications of Pangenomics:** 
• Pangenomics aids in identifying **genetic markers** for desirable traits, accelerating the breeding process. 
• It provides insights into the evolutionary history and genetic diversity of species, supporting conservation efforts. 
• In agriculture, pangenomics enables the development of crops with enhanced **nutritional value, stress tolerance, and disease resistance**. 
• **Future Prospects:** 
• Genomic advancements like pangenomics can revolutionize agriculture by addressing challenges such as **food security and climate resilience**. 
• They pave the way for precision agriculture, allowing farmers to optimize crop production based on genetic insights. </ul

questions.question: What is the name of the food pipe which takes food from the mouth to the stomach in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oesophagus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **oesophagus**, also known as the **food pipe**, is a **fibromuscular tube** approximately **25 centimetres** long that connects the **pharynx** (throat) to the **stomach**.
 
• It is located posterior to the **trachea** (windpipe) and anterior to the **vertebral column**, passing through the **diaphragm** at the **oesophageal hiatus**.
 
• The movement of food through the oesophagus is achieved via **peristalsis**, which involves rhythmic, **involuntary contractions** and relaxations of the smooth muscles.
 
• The **Lower Oesophageal Sphincter (LOS)** is a specialized bundle of muscles at the bottom of the pipe that acts as a valve to prevent **gastric acid** and stomach contents from flowing backward.
 
• The primary function of this organ is **transportation**; it does not involve the **chemical digestion** of food, which primarily begins in the mouth and continues in the stomach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bladder**:

 
 
• A hollow, muscular sac in the **pelvic cavity** that serves as a reservoir for **urine**.
 
• It is part of the **urinary system** and is connected to the **kidneys** via **ureters**.
 
 
 
• **Intestine**:
 
 
• Consists of the **Small Intestine**, where most **nutrient absorption** occurs, and the **Large Intestine**, which absorbs water and forms **feces**.
 
• It represents the longest part of the **alimentary canal**, measuring several meters in length.
 
 
 
• **Spleen**:
 
 
• A vital organ of the **lymphatic system** located in the upper left quadrant of the **abdomen**.
 
• Its main roles include filtering the **blood**, recycling old **red blood cells**, and storing **platelets** and white blood cells.

questions.question:
A car accelerates uniformly from rest to a speed of 20 m/s in 5 seconds.

What is the magnitude of its acceleration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 m/s²**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate of change of **velocity** of an object with respect to **time**.
 
• The formula to calculate **uniform acceleration** is derived from the **first equation of motion**: v = u + at, which can be rearranged as a = (v - u) / t.
 
• In this scenario, the car starts from **rest**, which means the **initial velocity (u)** is 0 m/s.
 
• The **final velocity (v)** reached by the car is 20 m/s, and the **time (t)** taken to reach this speed is 5 seconds.
 
• Plugging these values into the formula: a = (20 - 0) / 5.
 
• The calculation results in an acceleration of **4 m/s²**.
 
• Option (1) is incorrect as 20 / 5 is not 2. Option (3) and (4) are incorrect as they represent values derived from incorrect mathematical operations (like 20 / 2 or 5 squared).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **SI unit** of acceleration is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• Acceleration is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• If an object is slowing down, the acceleration is opposite to the direction of motion, often referred to as **retardation** or **deceleration**.
 
• **Uniform acceleration** implies that the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time, which is represented by a straight line on a **velocity-time graph**.
 
• The **slope** of a velocity-time graph gives the **magnitude of acceleration**.

questions.question:
Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): The Reusable Launch Vehicle - Technology Demonstrator (RLV-TD) program by ISRO is a cornerstone for India's future reusable space access capabilities.

Reason (R): RLV-TD missions are specifically designed to test crucial technologies like hypersonic flight, autonomous landing systems, and the structural resilience of a winged re-entry vehicle.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** is true because the **Reusable Launch Vehicle - Technology Demonstrator (RLV-TD)** is a series of technology demonstration missions that serve as the first step towards realizing a **Two-Stage-to-Orbit (TSTO)** fully reusable vehicle. It is considered a cornerstone because it aims to drastically reduce the cost of access to space by recycling the launch vehicle.
 
• **Reason (R)** is true because the primary objective of the **RLV-TD** program is to evaluate and validate various technologies. These include **hypersonic flight**, **autonomous landing**, **powered cruise flight**, and the use of **air-breathing propulsion**. The vehicle is designed to survive the high temperatures of **re-entry** using advanced thermal protection systems.
 
• **R is the correct explanation of A** because the successful testing and validation of these specific technologies (hypersonic flight, autonomous landing, and structural resilience) are exactly what make the **RLV-TD** program the foundational 'cornerstone' for India's future reusable space capabilities. Without mastering these technical aspects, a reusable system cannot be built.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first experimental flight of **RLV-TD**, known as the **HEX-01 (Hypersonic Flight Experiment)**, was successfully conducted by **ISRO** on **May 23, 2016**, from Sriharikota.
 
• In **April 2023**, ISRO successfully conducted the **RLV LEX (Landing Experiment)** at the Aeronautical Test Range in **Chitradurga, Karnataka**, where the vehicle performed an autonomous landing under conditions similar to a space re-entry.
 
• The ultimate goal of the **RLV** program is to bring down the cost of launching payloads into **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** to about 1/10th of the current cost, which is approximately **$20,000 per kg**.
 
• The configuration of **RLV-TD** resembles an aircraft, combining the complexity of both a **launch vehicle** and an **aircraft**.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios best illustrates the principle of conservation of momentum?

options.text: A ball rolling down a frictionless incline increases its speed.
A car comes to a stop when the brakes are applied due to friction.
When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils in the opposite direction.
A satellite maintains a stable orbit around the Earth due to gravity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils in the opposite direction**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Momentum** states that the total **linear momentum** of a closed or **isolated system** remains constant if no **external force** acts on it. Momentum is defined as the product of an object's **mass** and its **velocity**.
 
• **Statement 1:** A ball rolling down a **frictionless incline** increases its speed because of the **external force** of **gravity** acting along the slope. Since an external force is accelerating the ball, the **momentum** of the ball is not conserved; it increases as the **velocity** increases. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2:** When a car comes to a stop due to **brakes**, the **external force** of **friction** between the tires and the **road** acts on the vehicle. This force changes the **momentum** of the car from its initial value to **zero**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3:** When a **bullet** is fired from a **gun**, the system (gun + bullet) is initially at rest with a total **momentum** of **zero**. Upon firing, the **internal force** of the exploding gunpowder pushes the bullet forward and the gun backward. The forward **momentum** of the bullet is exactly balanced by the backward **recoil momentum** of the gun, keeping the total **system momentum** at **zero**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 4:** A **satellite** in a stable **orbit** is subject to the **external gravitational force** of the **Earth**. While the magnitude of its **velocity** (speed) might remain constant in a circular orbit, its direction is constantly changing due to **centripetal force**, meaning its **vector momentum** is continuously changing. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mathematical Expression:** The principle is mathematically represented as **m1u1 + m2u2 = m1v1 + m2v2**, where **m** represents **mass**, **u** represents **initial velocity**, and **v** represents **final velocity** of the interacting bodies.
 
• **Newton’s Third Law Connection:** The conservation of **momentum** is a direct consequence of **Newton’s Third Law of Motion**, which states that for every action, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**. The forces between the bullet and the gun are internal **action-reaction pairs**.
 
• **Types of Collisions:** In **physics**, momentum is conserved in both **elastic** and **inelastic collisions**. However, **kinetic energy** is only conserved in **elastic collisions** (like ideal **gas molecules** or **billiard balls**), while it is partially converted to **heat** or **sound** in inelastic ones.
 
• **Applications:** This principle is fundamental in **rocket propulsion**. A **rocket** moves upward by ejecting **exhaust gases** downward at high **velocity**. The downward **momentum** of the gases provides an equal upward **momentum** to the rocket body.
 
• **Vector Nature:** Since **velocity** is a **vector**, **momentum** is also a **vector quantity**. This means that in **two-dimensional** or **three-dimensional** space, the **momentum** must be conserved independently along the **x, y, and z axes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **System Definition:** For the conservation law to apply, one must clearly define the **isolated system**. In the gun-bullet example, if we only look at the bullet, its **momentum** is not conserved because the gun exerts a **force** on it. Conservation only applies when both objects are treated as a **single unit**.
 
• **Recoil Velocity:** The **recoil velocity** of a **gun** is much smaller than the **muzzle velocity** of the **bullet** because the **mass** of the gun is significantly larger than the **mass** of the bullet, as shown by the relation **V_gun = -(m_bullet * v_bullet) / M_gun**.
 
• **Impulse:** The change in **momentum** is known as **impulse**. When an **external force** is applied over a **time interval**, the **momentum** changes according to the **Impulse-Momentum Theorem** (**Force × Time = ΔMomentum**).
 
• **Historical Context:** While the concept of **momentum** was discussed by earlier scientists like **Descartes**, it was **Sir Isaac Newton** who formalized these laws in his work **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica** published in **1687**.

questions.question:
Read the following statements carefully:

Statement I: A pressure cooker operates by decreasing the pressure inside, which lowers the boiling point of water.

Statement II: Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because the higher pressure allows water to boil at a temperature above 100°C.

Statement III: The superheated steam within the cooker increases the rate of heat transfer to the food, leading to faster cooking.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.text: Only II and III are correct
All I, II, and III are correct
Only I and II are correct
Only I and III are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1 (Only II and III are correct)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement II:** Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because the higher pressure increases the boiling point of water above 100°C, enabling faster heat transfer to the food.
 
• **Statement III:** Superheated steam generated within the pressure cooker accelerates cooking due to enhanced heat transfer efficiency.
 
• **Statement I:** Incorrect, as a pressure cooker operates by increasing pressure inside, not decreasing it, which raises the boiling point of water.
 
• Pressure cooking is widely used to save time and energy while preparing food due to its efficient heat utilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boiling Point Elevation:** At higher pressure, water boils at temperatures above 100°C, allowing food to cook faster.
 
• **Superheated Steam:** Steam produced at elevated pressure carries more heat energy, leading to efficient cooking processes.
 
• **Working Principle:** Pressure cookers use sealed lids to trap steam, increasing internal pressure and temperature for faster cooking.
 
• **Thermodynamics:** The higher pressure and temperature improve thermal conductivity and heat absorption by the food inside.
 
• Pressure cooking reduces cooking times significantly compared to conventional methods, making it energy-efficient.

questions.question: The universal law of gravitation states that the gravitational force between two objects is proportional to ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the product of the masses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation**, formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687**, states that every point mass in the universe attracts every other point mass with a force directed along the line intersecting both points.
 
• The magnitude of this **gravitational force** is directly proportional to the **product of their masses** (m₁ × m₂). This means if the mass of one object doubles, the force of gravity between them also doubles.
 
• The law also specifies that the force is **inversely proportional** to the **square of the distance** (r²) between the centers of the two objects. This relationship is known as the **Inverse Square Law**.
 
• The complete mathematical formula for the law is F = G frac{m₁m₂}{r²} , where **F** represents the force, **m₁** and **m₂** are the masses, **r** is the separation distance, and **G** is the proportionality constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)**:

 
 
• The value of **G** is approximately **6.674 × 10−¹¹ Nm²/kg²**.
 
• Unlike the acceleration due to gravity (g), the value of **G** remains constant throughout the **universe**.
 
• It was first accurately measured by **Henry Cavendish** in his famous **Cavendish experiment** in **1798** using a torsion balance.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Gravitational Force**:
 
 
• It is a **conservative force**, meaning the work done is independent of the path taken.
 
• It is a **central force** that acts along the line joining the centers of gravity of the two bodies.
 
• Despite being the weakest of the four fundamental forces of nature, it governs the motion of **planets**, **stars**, and **galaxies** over long distances.
 
• It is always **attractive** and does not depend on the medium present between the two objects.

questions.question: The 'ossification test' is used to determine the__________. of a person.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Age**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• The **ossification test** is a scientific method used to determine the **age of a person** by studying the development and fusion of bones. 
 
• This test is based on the principle that the **human skeleton undergoes predictable changes** as a person grows older, with certain bones fusing at specific ages. 
 
• The process of **ossification**, or bone formation, begins in the fetus and continues into early adulthood, making it a reliable marker for age estimation. 
 
• It is commonly used in **forensic investigations**, **legal disputes** (such as determining the age of juveniles), and in fields like **anthropology** and **archaeology**. 
 
• The test typically involves X-ray imaging of bones like the **clavicle**, **pelvis**, **wrists**, and **long bones**, as these are key indicators of age-specific bone fusion patterns. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Stages of Ossification:** 
 
 
• **Primary ossification:** This process begins during the fetal stage and involves the formation of the bone's diaphysis (shaft). 
 
• **Secondary ossification:** This occurs after birth and includes the development of the epiphysis (ends of long bones). 
 
• The fusion of epiphyseal plates (growth plates) occurs at specific ages, providing key indicators for age estimation. 
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ossification Test:** 
 
 
• **Forensic Science:** Used to determine the age of unidentified bodies or suspects in legal cases. 
 
• **Sports:** Helps verify the age of athletes in age-restricted competitions. 
 
• **Legal Disputes:** Often employed in cases involving child labor, juvenile crime, and adoption to ascertain the true age of individuals. 
 
 
 
• **Accuracy:** 
 
 
• The ossification test is generally accurate but may vary slightly depending on factors like **genetics**, **nutrition**, and **environmental conditions**. 
 
• In some cases, advanced imaging techniques like **CT scans** and **MRI** are used to enhance accuracy. 
 
 
 
• **Limitations:** 
 
 
• It is less effective in adults as most bones are fully ossified by the age of 25. 
 
• Factors such as **malnutrition**, **hormonal disorders**, and **genetic anomalies** can affect the ossification process, leading to discrepancies in age determination. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Legal Use in India:** 
 
 
• In India, the ossification test is often used in court cases to determine the age of juveniles under the **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015**. 
 
• It is also used in cases of child labor to verify compliance with the **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986**. 
 
 
 
• **Bone Fusion Timelines:** 
 
 
• The **clavicle** is one of the last bones to ossify, completing its fusion around the age of 25. 
 
• In children, the **wrists** and **knees** are key indicators of bone age, as they show early ossification patterns. 
 
 
 
• **Global Relevance:** 
 
 
• The ossification test is recognized worldwide for its utility in forensic and legal contexts. 
 
• Different countries may have specific guidelines or protocols for conducting the test, ensuring its reliability and validity in various contexts.

questions.question: An electric kettle is rated 2.2kW 220V. It the cost of electricity is ₹4 per unit (kwh), what is the cost of boiling water for 30 minutes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹4.4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The electric kettle is rated **2.2kW**, which means it consumes 2.2 kilowatts of power per hour.
 
• Electricity cost is specified as ₹4 per unit (**1 unit = 1 kWh**).
 
• Boiling water for 30 minutes equates to **0.5 hours of usage**.
 
• Power consumption in 30 minutes is **2.2kW × 0.5 hours = 1.1 kWh**.
 
• Cost of electricity for 1.1 kWh is **₹4 × 1.1 = ₹4.4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unit of Power:** Power is measured in kilowatts (kW), and energy usage is calculated in kilowatt-hours (kWh).
 
• **Electricity Billing:** A unit (kWh) refers to the energy consumed when a device uses 1 kilowatt of power for 1 hour.
 
• **Cost Calculation:** The cost of electricity is determined by multiplying the energy consumed (kWh) by the rate per unit.
 
• **Efficiency Considerations:** Electric kettles are designed to convert electrical energy into heat with high efficiency, minimizing energy losses.
 
• **Daily Usage:** Understanding energy consumption helps households manage electricity bills effectively and promotes energy-saving practices.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unique characteristic of sponges (Phylum Porifera)?

options.text: Radial symmetry and presence of tentacles

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water canal system and choanocytes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sponges (Phylum Porifera) are characterized by the presence of a **water canal system**, which facilitates water circulation for feeding, respiration, and excretion.
 
• **Choanocytes**, or collar cells, are specialized cells in sponges responsible for creating water currents and trapping food particles.
 
• The water canal system includes structures such as **ostia (pores), spongocoel (central cavity), and osculum (exit opening)**, ensuring efficient water flow.
 
• Sponges lack tissues and organs but have a unique cellular organization that supports their **filter-feeding mechanism**.
 
• They exhibit **asymmetry or radial symmetry**, making them distinct from other animal phyla.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Choanocytes:**

 
 
• These are flagellated cells with a collar-like structure that helps in trapping food particles.
 
• Choanocytes are essential for the sponge's filter-feeding and water circulation.
 
 
 
• **Water Canal System:**
 
 
• It consists of pathways like ostia, spongocoel, and osculum through which water flows.
 
• The system aids in nutrient absorption, gas exchange, and waste removal.
 
 
 
• **Skeleton of Sponges:**
 
 
• Sponges possess a skeleton made of **spicules (calcium carbonate or silica) or spongin fibers**.
 
• These structures provide support and protection.
 
 
 
• **Reproduction in Sponges:**
 
 
• Sponges reproduce sexually via gametes and asexually via budding or gemmules.
 
• They are mostly hermaphroditic, with both male and female reproductive cells present in the same organism.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• Sponges play a crucial role in marine ecosystems as filter feeders, cleaning water and recycling nutrients.
 
• They also serve as habitats for various microorganisms and small marine organisms.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the goal of stem cell therapy in modern medicine?

options.text: To provide genetic immunity against viruses
To prevent blood clotting in arteries
To replace or regenerate damaged tissues or organs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To replace or regenerate damaged tissues or organs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Stem cell therapy** aims to replace or regenerate damaged tissues or organs, offering a potential cure for various debilitating diseases.
 
• Stem cells are unique because they have the ability to differentiate into various specialized cell types, such as muscle, nerve, or blood cells.
 
• This therapy is being extensively researched for conditions like **spinal cord injuries, diabetes, Parkinson’s disease, and heart disease**.
 
• Stem cells can be derived from **embryonic stem cells, adult stem cells, or induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs)**, providing multiple avenues for treatment.
 
• The goal is not just repair but also to restore normal function to damaged tissues or organs, which traditional medicine often cannot achieve.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stem Cells:**

 
 
• These are undifferentiated cells capable of dividing and renewing themselves over long periods.
 
• They have the ability to differentiate into specialized cell types.
 
• Two main types: **embryonic stem cells** (pluripotent) and **adult stem cells** (multipotent).
 
 
 
• **Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSCs):**
 
 
• iPSCs are adult cells reprogrammed to behave like embryonic stem cells.
 
• They eliminate ethical concerns associated with using embryonic stem cells.
 
• iPSCs are widely used in regenerative medicine and disease modeling.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Stem Cell Therapy:**
 
 
• Bone marrow transplants for blood disorders like leukemia.
 
• Potential treatments for neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s.
 
• Regeneration of damaged organs such as the heart, liver, or kidneys.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Stem Cell Therapy:**
 
 
• Ethical concerns regarding embryonic stem cells.
 
• High costs and complex procedures.
 
• Risks such as immune rejection or tumor formation.

questions.question: Which pathway in cellular respiration generates the most ATP?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Electron Transport Chain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electron transport chain (ETC)** is a crucial pathway in cellular respiration that generates the most **ATP (adenosine triphosphate).**
 
• It occurs in the inner membrane of the **mitochondria** in eukaryotic cells.
 
• The ETC uses high-energy electrons from molecules like **NADH and FADH₂**, which are produced during earlier stages of respiration.
 
• Electrons are transferred through a series of protein complexes, including **cytochromes**, which pump **protons (H⁺)** across the mitochondrial membrane, creating a **proton gradient.**
 
• This proton gradient powers the enzyme **ATP synthase** to synthesize ATP via a process called **oxidative phosphorylation.**
 
• The ETC is responsible for producing approximately **34 ATP molecules** per glucose molecule, making it the most efficient pathway in energy production.
 
• Oxygen acts as the final electron acceptor in the ETC, combining with protons and electrons to form **water**, which is essential to the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glycolysis**__

 __
 
• **Glycolysis** is the first step in cellular respiration, occurring in the **cytoplasm** of the cell.
 
• It breaks down **glucose** into two molecules of **pyruvate**, producing a net gain of **2 ATP** molecules and **2 NADH** molecules.
 
• Though it is an essential step, it generates far less ATP compared to the ETC.
 
 
 
• **Krebs Cycle**__
 __
 
• The **Krebs cycle**, also known as the **citric acid cycle**, occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
 
• It produces **NADH** and **FADH₂**, which are used in the electron transport chain.
 
• The cycle directly generates only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation**__
 
 
• **Fermentation** is an anaerobic process that occurs in the absence of oxygen.
 
• It produces ATP through **glycolysis** and regenerates **NAD+** for continued glycolysis.
 
• However, it generates only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule, making it far less efficient than aerobic respiration.

questions.question: Which technology is increasingly being used for real-time Air Quality Index (AQI) monitoring in urban areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Remote sensing and satellite data**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Remote sensing** and **satellite data** have become pivotal in monitoring the **Air Quality Index (AQI)** because they provide extensive spatial coverage that ground-based stations cannot achieve alone.
 
• Satellites equipped with advanced sensors can detect various atmospheric constituents such as **nitrogen dioxide (NO2)**, **sulfur dioxide (SO2)**, **carbon monoxide (CO)**, and **aerosols** (particulate matter).
 
• This technology allows for **real-time monitoring** and the tracking of long-range transport of pollutants across borders and oceans, which is essential for urban planning and public health warnings.
 
• **Seismic sensors** are used to detect and record **earthquakes** and ground vibrations; they have no application in measuring air chemistry.
 
• **Sonar technology** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) is primarily used for **underwater** exploration, navigation, and communication.
 
• **Ground penetrating radar (GPR)** is a geophysical method used to image **subsurface** structures and is commonly used in archaeology and engineering, not for atmospheric analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Copernicus Sentinel-5P** satellite, launched by the **European Space Agency (ESA)**, carries the **TROPOMI** instrument, which is specifically designed for high-resolution global air quality monitoring.
 
• In India, the **National Air Quality Index (AQI)** was launched in **October 2014** to disseminate information on air quality in an easily understandable format for the general public.
 
• The AQI considers eight major pollutants: **PM10**, **PM2.5**, **NO2**, **SO2**, **CO**, **O3** (Ozone), **NH3** (Ammonia), and **Pb** (Lead).
 
• **Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD)** is a critical parameter measured by satellites like **MODIS** (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) to estimate ground-level **PM2.5** concentrations.

questions.question: What are the products in a reaction where an acid reacts with a base?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A reaction in which an **acid** reacts with a **base** is termed a **Neutralization reaction**.
 
• In this process, the **hydrogen ions (H+)** from the acid and the **hydroxide ions (OH-)** from the base combine to form **water (H2O)**.
 
• The remaining part of the acid (anion) and the base (cation) combine to produce an **ionic compound** known as a **salt**.
 
• The general chemical equation for this reaction is: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**. ***Hence, the correct option is Salt and water.***
 
• Neutralization reactions are typically **exothermic**, meaning **heat** is evolved during the reaction, which often raises the temperature of the reaction mixture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of Neutralization:**

 
 
• The reaction between **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** produces **Sodium chloride (NaCl)** and **water**. The formula is: **HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O**.
 
• Another common example is the reaction between **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)** and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)** to form **Potassium sulfate (K2SO4)** and **water**.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Salts:**
 
 
• If a **strong acid** reacts with a **strong base**, the resulting salt is **neutral** (pH value of **7**).
 
• A **strong acid** reacting with a **weak base** produces an **acidic salt** (pH value **less than 7**).
 
• A **weak acid** reacting with a **strong base** results in a **basic salt** (pH value **greater than 7**).
 
 
 
• **Real-world Applications:**
 
 
• **Indigestion:** Our stomach produces **hydrochloric acid** to digest food. Excess acid causes **acidity**, which is neutralized by taking **antacids** like **Milk of Magnesia** (Magnesium hydroxide), which is a **base**.
 
• **Ant Stings:** The sting of an ant contains **formic acid**. The effect of the sting can be neutralized by rubbing moist **baking soda** (sodium hydrogen carbonate) or **calamine solution** (zinc carbonate), which are **basic** in nature.
 
• **Soil Treatment:** Plants do not grow well if the **soil** is too acidic or too basic. Acidic soil is treated with **bases** like **quicklime** (calcium oxide) or **slaked lime** (calcium hydroxide).
 
• **Factory Waste:** Many **factories** discharge acidic wastes. These are neutralized by adding **basic substances** before being disposed of into water bodies to protect **aquatic life**.

questions.question:
Read the statements carefully and select the correct option:

Assertion (A): Production of inorganic chemicals in India is centered in only northern states.

Reason (R): Sulphuric acid and soda ash are crucial chemicals in the production of fertilizers, detergents, and glass,

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is false, but R is true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Assertion (A) is false:** The production of inorganic chemicals in India is not centered only in northern states. It is distributed across various regions including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh, which are major hubs for chemical industries.
 
• **Reason (R) is true:** Sulphuric acid and soda ash are indeed crucial chemicals used in the production of fertilizers, detergents, and glass.
 
• Sulphuric acid is widely used in the manufacturing of fertilizers such as phosphate fertilizers. It is also utilized in petroleum refining and wastewater processing.
 
• Soda ash, also known as sodium carbonate, is a key ingredient in the production of glass, detergents, and other industrial products. India is a significant producer of soda ash, with Gujarat being a major contributor.
 
• Regions such as Gujarat and Maharashtra play a prominent role in inorganic chemical production due to favorable industrial infrastructure and proximity to raw materials.

• India's chemical industry is one of the largest globally and is divided into organic and inorganic chemicals.
 
• Inorganic chemicals, such as soda ash and sulphuric acid, are foundational for industries like fertilizers, detergents, and glass manufacturing.
 
• The presence of raw materials, proximity to ports, and industrial infrastructure influence the distribution of chemical production hubs across India.
